title: 2012 AMC 10A Problem 6
statement: The product of two positive numbers is \(9.\) The reciprocal of one of these numbers is \(4\) times the reciprocal of the other number. What is the sum of the two numbers?

solutions.text:
Let the two numbers be \(x\) and \(y\) such that \[ xy = 9 \text{ and } \dfrac{1}{x} = \dfrac{4}{y}. \]

We get that \[ y = \dfrac{9}{x} \]\[ \dfrac{1}{x} = \dfrac{4x}{9}. \]\[ x = \dfrac{3}{2}, \] since \(x\) is positive.

Then \[ y = 9 \div \dfrac{3}{2} = 6. \]

The desired sum is then \[ 6 + \dfrac{3}{2} = \dfrac{15}{2}. \]

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: Let the two numbers be \(x\) and \(y\)
Use \(xy=9\) and the reciprocal condition to relate \(x\) and \(y\)
